analysis:
The supplied files are changelog fragments and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md only, so there is no executable change to cite. The prose describes security-relevant behavior implemented elsewhere, and none of that source was supplied. I found no concrete regression.

Items for the next pass:
- GLM-5.3-Flash is now served in coordinator-connected mode (changelog glm53-native-prerequisites.md:14). It adds the runtime capability `glm5_next_v1`, a hardware gate, a 262,144-token context enforcement, catalog/revision-receipt/aggregate agreement, and a mandatory reviewed chat template. Unverified: that the coordinator-side capability and aggregate checks exist and that provider self-reported capabilities are not trusted for routing (TB-002, TB-009, TB-011).
- The encrypted SSD prefix store defaults on for the pinned GLM identity (line 9). Media rows reportedly never reuse cached prefixes (lines 11, video fragment). This extends T-041/SEC-035 to GLM. The TTL, HMAC naming and salt scoping must be confirmed unchanged.
- A DEBUG-only `DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE` persistent cache key is described (line 21). Confirm it is compiled out of release builds, since it would bypass the SE-rooted KEK (T-041, A-003).
- New untrusted-input surfaces: inline video decode (`data:video/mp4`) and image decode of consumer media. Confirm bounded memory (512 MiB frame cap, 28,532-token cap) and the parser's malformed-input handling (T-050 class, DoS).
- Local Responses `previous_response_id` retains plaintext prompt history in memory. The LRU history is bounded, but the SDK response-object store has no matching eviction (hardware-support.md head lines 35-42). This is a local-mode A-001 retention and memory-growth question. Check whether coordinator-connected mode can reach it.
- Weight hashing now uses F_NOCACHE aligned reads (T-012/T-027). Digests are claimed unchanged; verify there is no TOCTOU or skipped-region regression.
- New retained-fault metrics are exposed on local /metrics. Confirm no sensitive data and no remote exposure.
- Docs mention HTTP 503 capacity rejection before headers. Confirm no side channel.
